anchor: some romantic incident implying
note: Romantic: here, belonging to a made-up adventure story.

anchor: anterior to catching sight of him
note: Anterior: earlier, coming before in time.

anchor: whatever of enigma may appear to lurk in the case
note: Enigma: a puzzle or mystery.

anchor: that prime element of Radcliffian romance, the mysterious
note: Ann Radcliffe wrote Gothic novels full of mystery, such as The Mysteries of Udolpho (1794). Melville says Claggart’s motive is as mysterious as hers.

anchor: an antipathy spontaneous and profound
note: Antipathy: a deep dislike felt without cause, as Claggart feels.

anchor: no irritating juxtaposition of dissimilar personalities
note: Juxtaposition: placing things side by side. A ship forces very different men to live together.

anchor: give it Jonah’s toss
note: In the Book of Jonah, sailors threw Jonah overboard to calm a storm sent on his account.
source: The Bible (King James Version), Jonah 1:15, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/10

anchor: the direct reverse of a saint
note: Claggart is imagined as the opposite of a saint.

anchor: the deadly space between
note: A quoted phrase for the gulf between a normal mind and one like Claggart’s.

anchor: this is best done by indirection
note: Indirection: approaching a subject by roundabout means.

anchor: a nut not be cracked by the tap of a lady’s fan
note: The scholar means X is a hard nut to crack, not to be understood by a light touch.

anchor: the adherent of no organized religion
note: Adherent: a follower or supporter.

anchor: enter his labyrinth
note: A labyrinth is a maze, here a mind hard to enter and leave.

anchor: a superficial knowledge of it
note: Superficial: shallow, only on the surface.

anchor: the dotage of senile love
note: Dotage: foolish weakness from old age. Senile: showing the weakness of age.

anchor: Coke and Blackstone hardly shed so much light
note: Sir Edward Coke (1552 to 1634) wrote the Institutes and Sir William Blackstone wrote the Commentaries on the laws of England. Both were standard law books.
source: Encyclopædia Britannica, 11th ed. (1911), “Coke, Sir Edward”, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/1911_Encyclop%C3%A6dia_Britannica/Coke%2C_Sir_Edward; Encyclopædia Britannica, 11th ed. (1911), “Blackstone, Sir William”, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/1911_Encyclop%C3%A6dia_Britannica/Blackstone%2C_Sir_William

anchor: Mostly recluses
note: Recluses: people who live alone, away from society.

anchor: if that lexicon which is based on Holy Writ were any longer popular
note: Lexicon: a dictionary, here the vocabulary of the Bible. Holy Writ: the Bible.

anchor: denominate certain phenomenal men
note: Denominate: to name or classify.

anchor: tinctured with the Biblical element
note: Tinctured: slightly colored or influenced.

anchor: In a list of definitions included in the authentic translation of Plato
note: The Definitions are a list of terms once printed with Plato’s works but written by later hands.

anchor: “Natural Depravity: a depravity according to nature.”
note: Depravity: moral corruption. The definition means a corruption that is part of one’s nature.

anchor: tho’ savoring of Calvinism
note: John Calvin (1509 to 1564) taught that humans are born corrupt. Calvinism is the Protestant system built on his teaching.

anchor: by no means involves Calvin’s dogmas as to total mankind
note: Dogmas: formal beliefs. Calvin held that all people are depraved. Melville says natural depravity applies only to a few.

anchor: have no vulgar alloy of the brute in them
note: Alloy: an impure mixture. These men have nothing coarse or animal in them.

anchor: Civilization, especially if of the austerer sort, is auspicious to it
note: Auspicious: favorable. Strict civilization encourages hidden evil.

anchor: It never allows wine to get within its guard
note: A man of this sort never drinks enough to lose control.

anchor: anything mercenary or avaricious
note: Mercenary: motivated by money. Avaricious: greedy.

anchor: partakes nothing of the sordid or sensual
note: Sordid: dirty, morally low. Sensual: pleasure-seeking.

anchor: free from acerbity
note: Acerbity: sharpness, bitterness in manner.

anchor: signalizes so exceptional a nature
note: Signalizes: marks out as notable.

anchor: an ambidexter implement for effecting the irrational
note: Ambidexter: working with either hand, serving both sides. Reason serves the irrational purpose.

anchor: in wantonness of malignity
note: Wantonness: reckless, willful behavior. Malignity: deep ill will.

anchor: sagacious and sound
note: Sagacious: shrewd and wise, used here for a cool mind.

anchor: the mania of an evil nature
note: Mania: madness, an extreme obsession.

anchor: licentious living
note: Licentious: lacking moral restraint, especially sexually.

anchor: Why not subpoena as well the clerical proficients?
note: Subpoena: a court order to appear and testify. Melville jokes that priests should testify too.

anchor: mysteries of iniquity
note: From the Bible, Paul says “the mystery of iniquity doth already work,” meaning evil works in secret.
source: The Bible (King James Version), 2 Thessalonians 2:7, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/10

anchor: vindicate, as it may, its own credibility
note: Vindicate: prove right. Credibility: believability.
